chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, on the authority of Abdul Azeem al-Hasani, on the authority of Sulaiman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:

Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) used to call his son Ali (peace be upon him) 'al-Rida.' He would say, 'Call my son al-Rida for me,' 'I said to my son al-Rida,' and 'My son al-Rida said to me.' And when he addressed him, he would say, 'O Aba al-Hasan.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Aba al-Hasan (Father of Hasan), an honorific address used for Imam al-Rida
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (The Pleasing One / The Chosen One), a title of Imam Ali ibn Musa (as)
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ: Musa ibn Ja'far (as), known as Imam Kazim (as), father of Imam al-Rida

ai.seo_question: Why is Imam Ali ibn Musa (as) called al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the intimate familial bond between Musa al-Kazim and his son Ali, demonstrating that 'al-Rida' was an affectionate, personal title used within the household before becoming a public honorific. The specific usage of 'Aba al-Hasan' by Ali reinforces the dual legacy of the Imams, linking Ali ibn Musa to both his father Musa (Kazim) and the broader Ahl al-Bayt lineage through the name Hasan. This context underscores the Shia scholarly view that titles often reflect spiritual status and familial love, serving as a bridge between the hidden and public identities of the Imams.
